messages:
maria (devex): heads up — got two support tickets where `redwoodctl login` prints success but no profile/token ends up in the user's home on WSL2. both on Win10 + WSL2. anyone seen this?
jon (devex): hmm, saw one like this last week. user launched from Windows explorer and used the desktop shortcut. redwoodctl said "saved token to ~/.config/redwood/profiles/default.json" but file absent.
sam (eng-platform): quick q — are these installs via the Windows MSI or via brew on WSL?
maria (devex): MSI -> PATH shim -> launched from Explorer/Start menu. not run from a real login shell.
kai (eng-runtime): likely XDG_CONFIG_HOME / HOME pointing at a mounted C: path when launched that way. perms and mount options can make writes fail silently. do we swallow write errors?
jon (devex): in both repros the user didn't see an error. CLI printing success is the UX bug.
alex (devops): can you paste the small repro steps? i'll test quick in my WSL.
maria (devex): repro: 1) Windows MSI install 2) Start menu -> run redwoodctl login (opens browser) 3) CLI prints success and token path 4) open WSL home -> file missing.
ci-bot: automated note: attached logs from first report (redact token): 
```
INFO  redwoodctl/auth.go:142 Saved token to /mnt/c/Users/alex/.config/redwood/profiles/default.json
INFO  redwoodctl/cli.go:88 login completed
```

sam (eng-platform): interesting: path is /mnt/c/Users/alex/.config/... so redwoodctl was resolving HOME to the Windows profile mount. if the binary runs as the shim under Windows context, it writes to the windows-hosted path which may not be visible from WSL user's native $HOME.
kai (eng-runtime): two issues to cover: 1) the binary should warn when target path is outside the current OS user's native FS (e.g. /mnt/c), 2) installation path detection needs to prefer unix-homed user's XDG when executed in WSL.
jon (devex): short-term workaround for affected users: run `env HOME="$HOME" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config" redwoodctl login` from inside WSL shell (explicitly shell-run). or `redwoodctl login --headless` and pipe token to `redwoodctl profile import -` (if we accept token import).
maria (devex): i patched a quick helper for support: `if [ -f /proc/version ] && grep -qi microsoft /proc/version; then export RWCTL_PREFER_WSL_HOME=1; fi` — works but hacky.
alex (devops): i repro'd. when launched from windows shim the process env HOME is set to /mnt/c/Users/username. writing to that path as WSL user sometimes requires metadata/uid translations and ends up failing with EACCES in some setups. CLI swallowed the write error.
jon (devex): actionable items: - make `redwoodctl login` fail noisily if token write fails - add a check and friendly message when HOME or XDG_CONFIG_HOME points to a mount under /mnt/c (or other foreign mount) - doc troubleshooting: WSL gotchas.
sam (eng-platform): agree. add a telemetry event for failed write attempts so we can quantify. also add `--output-token-file` flag for headless flows.
kai (eng-runtime): i'll send a small PR: 1) wrap write with explicit error check and nonzero exit 2) detect linux-on-wsl via /proc/version and prefer Linux native home if present, but only when we know the process is running inside WSL. default still respects env vars.
maria (devex): can we also add a CLI hint: "If you're on WSL and launched from Start menu, run from a WSL shell to persist tokens"? short message.
alex (devops): yes. also add docs note about antimalware blocking writes to /mnt/c sometimes. seen that too.
jon (devex): cool. i'll file an issue with repro notes and attach ci-bot logs. assigning to kai for the runtime patch and sam for telemetry/flag.
ci-bot: issue created: GH#4587 — "redwoodctl login silently reports success when token can't be written on WSL/Windows shim"
maria (devex): thanks y'all. quick support workaround to paste in tickets: 1) open WSL shell 2) run `redwoodctl login` there 3) verify `ls -la ~/.config/redwood/profiles` 4) if still missing, run `redwoodctl login --headless` and `redwoodctl profile import -` with token. paste those 3 lines as the answer. :sparkles:
jon (devex): :thumbsup: closing thread once PR merges.
